stem:
The displacements of two sinusoidal waves propagating through a string are given by the following equations
\( y_1 = 4 \sin (20x - 30t) \)
\( y_2 = 4 \sin (25x - 40t) \)
where \( x \) and \( y \) are in centimeter and \( t \) is in second.
a) Calculate the phase difference between these two waves at the points \( x = 5 \) cm and \( t = 2 \) s.
b) When these two waves interfere, what are the maximum and minimum values of the intensity?
solution:
Given \( y_1 = 4 \sin (20x - 30t) \) and \( y_2 = 4 \sin (25x - 40t) \)

a) To find phase difference when \( x = 5 \) cm and \( t = 2 \) s:
\( y_1 = 4 \sin (20 \times 5 - 30 \times 2) = 4 \sin (100 - 60) = 4 \sin 40 \)
\( y_2 = 4 \sin (25 \times 5 - 40 \times 2) = 4 \sin (125 - 80) = 4 \sin 45 \)
\( \therefore \) Phase difference is 5 radian because \( \varphi = |45 - 40| = 5 \) radian.

b) To find the maximum and minimum values of the intensity:
Amplitudes of the two waves are \( A_1 = 4 \) cm and \( A_2 = 4 \) cm,
\( \therefore I_{\max} = (A_1 + A_2)^2 = (4 + 4)^2 = 64 \) when the phase difference is zero
and \( I_{\min} = (A_1 - A_2)^2 = (4 - 4)^2 = 0 \) when the phase difference is \( \pi \).

stem: A progressive wave travels on a stretched string. A particle on this string takes 4.0 ms to move from its mean position to one of its extreme positions. The distance between two consecutive points on the string which are at their mean positions (at a certain time instant) is 2.0 cm. Find the frequency, wavelength and speed of the wave.
solution:
A particle takes \( 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \) s to travel from its mean position to extreme position. This is a quarter of the complete oscillation as shown in Fig. (a). Hence, the particle will take \( 4 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \) s \( = 16 \times 10^{-3} \) s to complete one oscillation.
\( \therefore \) frequency \( n = 1/T = (1/16) \times 10^{3}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1} = 62.5 \) Hz

As shown in Fig. (b), points A, B, and C correspond to mean positions, but the string is moving in one direction at point A and in the opposite direction at point B. Thus, out of the two consecutive particles at their mean positions, one will be moving upwards while the other will be moving downwards. The distance between them is 2.0 cm. Therefore distance between two consecutive particles moving in the same direction will be \( 2 \times 2 \) cm \( = 4 \) cm. Thus the wavelength \( \lambda = 4 \) cm \( = 0.04 \) m
Speed of wave \( \mathrm{v} = n \times \lambda = 62.5 \times 0.04 = 2.5 \) m/s.

stem: Find the distance between two successive nodes in a stationary wave on a string vibrating with frequency 64 Hz. The velocity of progressive wave that resulted in the stationary wave is \( 48\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \).
solution:
Given:
Speed of wave \( = \mathrm{v} = 48\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \)
Frequency \( n = 64 \) Hz
We have \( \mathrm{v} = n\lambda \)
\( \therefore \lambda = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{n} = \dfrac{48}{64} = 0.75\ \mathrm{m} \)
We know that distance between successive nodes
\( = \dfrac{\lambda}{2} = \dfrac{0.75}{2} = 0.375 \) m

stem: An air column is of length 17 cm long. Calculate the frequency of 5th overtone if the air column is (a) closed at one end and (b) open at both ends. (Velocity of sound in air \( = 340\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1} \)).
solution:
Given
Length of air column \( = 17 \) cm \( = 0.17 \) m
Overtone number \( p = 5 \) and velocity of sound in air \( = 340\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1} \).

For an air column closed at one end,
Fundamental frequency \( n^{c} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{4L} = \dfrac{340}{4 \times 0.17} = 500 \) Hz
and frequency of \( p^{\text{th}} \) overtone \( n^{c}_{p} = (2p + 1)\, n^{c} \)
\( \therefore \) for fifth overtone \( n^{c}_{5} = (2 \times 5 + 1) \times 500 = 5500\ \mathrm{Hz} \)

For an air column open at both ends,
Fundamental frequency \( n^{o} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{2L} = \dfrac{340}{2 \times 0.17} \), \( n = 1000 \) Hz
and frequency of \( p^{\text{th}} \) overtone \( n^{o}_{p} = (p + 1)\, n^{o} \)
\( \therefore \) for fifth overtone \( n^{o}_{5} = (5 + 1) \times 1000 \), \( n^{o}_{5} = 6000\ \mathrm{Hz} \)

stem: A closed pipe and an open pipe have the same length. Show that no mode of the closed pipe has the same wavelength as any mode of the open pipe.
solution:
For a closed pipe, the frequency of allowed modes is given by \( n^{c}_{p} = (2p + 1)\, n^{c} \) where \( n^{c} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{4L} \) (superscript c and o refer to closed and open pipes respectively) using Eqs. (6.21) and (6.16), where \( p \) is any integer.
\( \therefore \lambda^{c}_{p} = \dfrac{4L}{2p + 1} \), where \( p \) is any integer.

On the other hand, for an open pipe, the frequency of allowed modes is given by, \( n^{o}_{m} = (m + 1)\, n^{o} \) and \( n^{o} = \mathrm{v}/2L \), using Eqs. (6.28) and (6.23), where \( m \) is any integer.
\( \therefore \lambda^{o}_{m} = \dfrac{2L}{m + 1} \)

If \( \lambda^{c}_{p} = \lambda^{o}_{m} \), it would mean \( \dfrac{4L}{2p + 1} = \dfrac{2L}{m + 1} \).
Or, \( 2(m + 1) = 2p + 1 \) which is not possible. Hence the two pipes cannot have modes with the same frequency or wavelength.

subtopic: Vibrations of a Stretched String and Sonometer
stem: A string is fixed at both ends. What is the ratio of the frequency of the first harmonic to that of the second harmonic?
solution:
For a string of length \( l \) fixed at both ends, the wavelengths of the first and second harmonics are given as \( l = \lambda/2 \) and \( l = \lambda_1 \) respectively. Hence the ratio of their frequencies is
\( \dfrac{n}{n_1} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}/\lambda}{\mathrm{v}/\lambda_1} = \dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{l}{2l} = \dfrac{1}{2} \)

subtopic: Vibrations of a Stretched String and Sonometer
stem: The velocity of a transverse wave on a string of length 0.5 m is 225 m/s. (a) What is the fundamental frequency of a standing wave on this string if both ends are kept fixed? (b) While this string is vibrating in the fundamental harmonic, what is the wavelength of sound produced in air if the velocity of sound in air is 330 m/s?
solution:
The wavelength of the fundamental mode is \( \lambda = 2l \), hence the fundamental frequency is
\( n = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{\lambda} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{2l} = \dfrac{225\ \mathrm{m/s}}{2 \times 0.5\ \mathrm{m}} = 225\ \mathrm{s}^{-1} = 225 \) Hz

While the string is vibrating in the fundamental harmonic, the frequency of the sound produced by the string will be same as the fundamental frequency of the string. The wavelength of sound produced is
\( = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}_s}{n} = \dfrac{330\ \mathrm{m/s}}{225\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}} = 1.467 \) m.

subtopic: Vibrations of a Stretched String and Sonometer
stem: A string 105 cm long is fixed at one end. Transverse vibrations of frequency 15 Hz are imposed at the free end. A stationary wave, produced in the string, consists of 3 loops. Calculate the speed of progressive waves which have produced the stationary wave in the string.
solution:
Given
Length of string \( = l = 105 \) cm \( = \) 3 loops
\( \therefore l = 3\dfrac{\lambda}{2} \)
\( \therefore \lambda = \dfrac{2}{3} l = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 105 = 70\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.70 \) m
Speed of wave \( = \mathrm{v} = n\lambda \)
\( \mathrm{v} = 15 \times 0.70 = 10.50\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \)

subtopic: Vibrations of a Stretched String and Sonometer
stem: A sonometer wire of length 50 cm is stretched by keeping weights equivalent of 3.5 kg. The fundamental frequency of vibration is 125 Hz. Determine the linear density of the wire.
solution:
Given, \( l = 50 \) cm \( = 0.5 \) m, \( T = 3.5 \) kg \( \times\ 9.8\ \mathrm{m/s}^{2} = 34.3 \) N, \( n = 125 \) Hz
\( n = \dfrac{1}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}} \)
\( \therefore n^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4l^{2}}\dfrac{T}{m} \)
\( \therefore m = \dfrac{T}{4n^{2}l^{2}} \)
\( \therefore m = \dfrac{34.3}{4 \times (125)^{2} \times (0.5)^{2}} \)
\( \therefore m = 2.195 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{kg\ m}^{-1} \)

subtopic: Vibrations of a Stretched String and Sonometer
stem: Two wires of the same material and the same cross section are stretched on a sonometer in succession. Length of one wire is 60 cm and that of the other is 30 cm. An unknown load is applied to the first wire and second wire is loaded with 1.5 kg. If both the wires vibrate with the same fundamental frequencies, calculate the unknown load.
solution:
Two wires are given to be of the same material and having the same cross section,
\( \therefore m_1 = m_2 = m \)
Same fundamental frequency, \( n_1 = n_2 = n \)
\( l_1 = 60 \) cm \( = 0.6 \) m, \( l_2 = 30 \) cm \( = 0.3 \) m, \( T_2 = 1.5 \times 9.8 \) N
For the first wire, \( n_1 = \dfrac{1}{2l_1}\sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{m_1}} \)
For the second wire, \( n_2 = \dfrac{1}{2l_2}\sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{m_2}} \)
\( \therefore \dfrac{n_1}{n_2} = \dfrac{l_2}{l_1}\sqrt{\dfrac{T_1 \times m_2}{T_2 \times m_1}} \)
\( \therefore \dfrac{n}{n} = \dfrac{0.3}{0.6}\sqrt{\dfrac{T_1 \times m}{1.5 \times 9.8 \times m}} \)
\( \therefore 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{1.5 \times 9.8}} \)
\( \therefore 2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{1.5 \times 9.8}} \)
or, \( 4 = \dfrac{T_1}{1.5 \times 9.8} \)  \( \therefore T_1 = 6 \times 9.8 \) N
\( \therefore \) Applied load \( = 6 \) kg.

subtopic: Vibrations of a Stretched String and Sonometer
stem: A wire has linear density \( 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \) kg/m. It is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of 360 N. The wire resonates at a frequency of 420 Hz and 490 Hz in two successive modes. Find the length of the wire.
solution:
Given \( m = 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \) kg/m, \( T = 360 \) N. Let the wire vibrate at 420 Hz and 490 Hz in its \( p^{\text{th}} \) and \( (p+1)^{\text{th}} \) harmonics. Then \( n_{p} = p \cdot n \) where \( n = \dfrac{1}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}} \) is the fundamental frequency
\( 420\ \mathrm{Hz} = \dfrac{p}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}} \) and \( 490\ \mathrm{Hz} = \dfrac{p+1}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}} \)
\( \therefore \dfrac{490}{420} = \dfrac{p+1}{p} \)
or, \( p = 6 \)
Using this value of \( p \), for the frequency of \( p^{\text{th}} \) harmonic, we get
\( 420\ \mathrm{Hz} = \dfrac{6}{2l}\sqrt{\dfrac{360\ \mathrm{N}}{4.0 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{kg/m}}} = \dfrac{900}{l}\ \mathrm{m/s} \)
\( \therefore l = 900/420\ \mathrm{m} = 2.143 \) m

stem: Two sound waves having wavelengths 81 cm and 82.5 cm produce 8 beats per second. Calculate the speed of sound in air.
solution:
Given
\( \lambda_1 = 81\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.81 \) m
\( \lambda_2 = 82.5\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.825 \) m
\( n_1 = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{\lambda_1} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{0.81} \)
\( n_2 = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{\lambda_2} = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{0.825} \)
Here \( \lambda_1 < \lambda_2 \), \( \therefore n_1 > n_2 \).
As 8 beats are produced per second,
\( n_1 - n_2 = 8 \)
\( \therefore \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{\lambda_1} - \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{\lambda_2} = 8 \)
\( \therefore \mathrm{v}\left[\dfrac{1}{\lambda_1} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_2}\right] = 8 \)
\( \therefore \mathrm{v}\left[\dfrac{1}{0.81} - \dfrac{1}{0.825}\right] = 8 \)
\( \therefore \mathrm{v} = 356.4 \)

stem: Two tuning forks having frequencies 320 Hz and 340 Hz are sounded together to produce sound waves. The velocity of sound in air is \( 326.4\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \). Find the difference in wavelength of these waves.
solution:
Given
\( n_1 = 320 \) Hz, \( n_2 = 340 \) Hz, \( \mathrm{v} = 326.4\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \).
\( \mathrm{v} = n_1\lambda_1 = n_2\lambda_2 \)
Here, \( n_1 < n_2 \), \( \therefore \lambda_1 > \lambda_2 \)
\( \therefore \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{n_1} - \dfrac{\mathrm{v}}{n_2} \)
\( \therefore \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = \mathrm{v}\left[\dfrac{1}{n_1} - \dfrac{1}{n_2}\right] \)
\( \therefore \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = 326.4\left[\dfrac{1}{320} - \dfrac{1}{340}\right] \)
\( \therefore \lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = 0.06 \) m
